title: UFO Video in Latest Drop of Defense Department Was Featured in 1956 Docudrama, Despite Claims It's Never Been Seen Before
excerpt: A video featured in the Trump administration's latest tranche of UFO files has actually been around for decades, and even received the Hollywood treatment, despite claims it was a "never-before-seen" clip.
content:
Tom Durante

Fri, September 18, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC

A video featured in the Trump administration’s latest tranche of UFO files appears to have been around for decades, and even received the Hollywood treatment, despite claims it was a “never-before-seen” clip.

The video was “revealed” on Friday as part of an exclusive Fox News segment by senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy.

“I was summoned to an office in the West Wing yesterday for a private briefing about these files you are about to see on your screen for the first time ever,” an excited Doocy told the curvy couch co-hosts on Friday morning.

He added: “It looks like a drone swarm, but there were no known drones when this was taken — in 1952! I’m told they took the first and only copy of this film. They found it in the National Archives. It has been digitized into 4K to be released right here for the first time today.”

But unfortunately for Doocy and the Defense Department, the 1952 video from Navy aerial photographer Delbert Newhouse, taken along a Utah highway, has been seen before. In fact, it was featured in a 1956 docudrama called Unidentified Flying Objects: The True Story of Flying Saucers.

The film can be seen on YouTube.

The movie features Newhouse talking about the morning he recorded the video while working for the U.S. Navy.

“I was driving on U.S. Highway 30 south with my wife and our son Delbert and our daughter Ann,” Newhouse says. “We were on our way from Washington, D.C., to Portland, Oregon, on vacation before reporting to my new duty station.”

He went on to describe the 12 objects “in a rough formation, proceeding in a westerly direction.”

When asked what the UFOs looked like, Newhouse said, “Two saucers, one inverted over the other.”

Newhouse’s footage is seen later in the film (at the 1:00:41 mark), after an analysis to determine its authenticity.

A 1956 article about the film from UPI notes that one of the Unidentified Flying Objects producers, Clarence Greene, was able to obtain “two pieces of motion picture film allegedly showing saucers that had been turned over to the government.”

While the quality of the footage in the movie is dated and grainy compared to the enhanced version released by the Defense Department on Friday, it appears to be the same floating orbs featured on Fox & Friends.

“We are not providing any comment or assessment on the files overall or on any specific file, so that the American people can make their own determinations regarding the files,” a Defense Department spokeswoman said in a statement to Mediaite.
